components.text: The alleged alignment is treated as a correlation between distinct phenomenal and neural events requiring explanation.
Whether pain's phenomenal, normative, and neural-functional roles form an independent correlation requiring explanation.
Whether naturalism selects among independently variable phenomenal-to-physical mappings.
Pleasure-pain inversion is offered as a genuine epistemic alternative contributing to naturalistic improbability.
Whether inverted pain and pleasure mappings belong to the relevant epistemic alternative space.
Whether pain's avoidance role is contingent or constrained by pain's nature.
Harmony is claimed to have low likelihood on naturalism because many disharmonious psychophysical mappings are available.
Whether harmony is unlikely conditional on the relevant naturalistic theory.
Whether the comparative likelihood calculation favors theism once identity naturalism is specified.
Identity naturalism allegedly removes the independent correlation and thereby the relevant explanatory or likelihood problem.
Identity theory is claimed to make harmony certain rather than epistemically unlikely.
Whether metaphysical identity makes harmony epistemically likely rather than merely metaphysically necessary.
Whether identity eliminates the epistemic space of alternative phenomenal-physical correlations.
An epistemic gap is claimed to preserve a probability distribution over alternative psychophysical correlations.
Many available mappings are invoked to support low naturalistic likelihood.
Whether an epistemically open possibility space supports a principled distribution of comparative likelihoods.
Whether numerous alternatives establish low naturalistic probability without a justified measure.
Sparse or ignorance-based backgrounds allegedly cannot support meaningful likelihood comparisons without an arbitrary prior measure.
Whether sparse evidential backgrounds can legitimately support comparative likelihood judgments.
The evidential issue should be prosecuted through sparse-background Bayesian likelihoods analogous to arguments from suffering.
How theism and naturalism should be comparatively evaluated when sparse-background likelihoods lack grounding.
Whether epistemic possibility distributions should control comparison of the complete theories.
Without a principled numerical distribution or privileged measure, no meaningful comparative likelihood judgment is available.
Measure difficulties motivate replacing local likelihood comparison with complete-theory assessment.
Whether absence of a precise or uniquely privileged measure defeats all comparative likelihood ordering.
Whether ordinal likelihood evidence can remain informative alongside broader theory comparison.
Pain's generic causal and rationalizing connection to aversive behavior is claimed to constrain inversion a priori.
Whether pain without avoidance behavior is epistemically incoherent or excluded a priori.
Conceivable pain-without-avoidance cases are offered against the alleged necessary pain-avoidance connection.
Whether isolated pain-without-avoidance scenarios defeat the generic necessary connection.
Whether normative harmony requires an exceptionless pain-avoidance alignment.
A necessary generic pain-avoidance connection is claimed to survive the admission of exceptional pain-without-avoidance cases.
Whether admitting intrinsic outliers permits a world in which the pain-avoidance generic itself fails.
Intrinsic duplicates of an admitted outlier can allegedly be freely recombined into an epistemically possible counterexample world.
Whether intrinsic outliers may be freely recombined into an epistemically possible outlier-only world.
Strong reductive identity is claimed to eliminate the independent harmony relation and thereby undermine the pro argument.
Modal constructions require independent justification rather than following automatically from epistemic possibility.
Whether reductive identity eliminates all force from the harmony argument.
Whether an epistemic gap preserves likelihood comparison despite metaphysical identity.
The closing qualification treats reductive consciousness chiefly as a condition that limits the harmony argument against naturalism.
Whether reductive materialism marks a contrast between naturalism and theism.
